full_name: Margaret Litvin | Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University
title: 2021–2022 Humanities Hilles Bush Fellow Boston University
bio: Margaret Litvin, an associate professor of Arabic and comparative literature at Boston University, studies the transnational entanglements of modern Arabic literature and theater. Her first book, Hamlet’s Arab Journey: Shakespeare’s Prince and Nasser’s Ghost (Princeton University Press, 2011), has appeared on syllabi for courses on theater history, comparative literature, and anthropology of the Middle East. Her translations from Arabic include Sonallah Ibrahim’s Moscow-set novel Ice (Seagull, 2019) and several plays. With the historians Eileen Kane and Masha Kirasirova, she coedited Russian-Arab Worlds: A Documentary History (Oxford University Press, forthcoming).
